title: Scripture names them just before God himself
source_text: XII. Quandoquidem autem Scriptura Dei vox est, ex eo quod fideles a justitia ipsis inhaerente sanctos & justos denominat, certum est illos tales apud Deum cen-seri, & revera sanctos atque justos esse, non solum coram hominibus, & eorum opinione; sed etiam Dei ipsius judicio. Id docet manifeste Lucas, dum de Zacha-ria atque Elizabeth parentibus Joannis Baptistae testatur Ambos illos fuisse justos in conspectu Dei, incedentes in omnibus praeceptis & constitutionibus Domini inculpate, Luc. 1. 6.
pass_a_gloss: But since Scripture is the voice of God, from the fact that it denominates believers holy and just from the righteousness inherent in them it is certain that they are so reckoned before God, and are truly holy and just, not only before men and in their opinion, but also in the judgment of God himself. Luke teaches this plainly when he testifies of Zechariah and Elizabeth, the parents of John the Baptist, that both of them were just in the sight of God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blamelessly (Luke 1:6).
pass_b_english: Because Scripture is God's voice, those it names just from inherent righteousness are truly such before God, not only before men.
Luke 1:6: Zechariah and Elizabeth were just before God.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1046.
